title: Field Map
description: A playable region: the scale at which the player actually walks. Sits under a region and above its points of interest. The terrain is generated from `seed_biomes` by the game's own generator; canon does not describe tiles, only what the place is and what is worth finding in it.

region.description: Region entity id this belongs to.

seed_biomes.description: The biome palette the generator draws terrain from, in rough order of dominance. Ids come from database/biomes.json. This is the only thing canon says about terrain -- layout is the engine's business.

scale.description: Small maps carry 5-8 points of interest and are learnable in a session; large ones 10-20 with several ecological zones.

points_of_interest.description: point_of_interest ids placed on this map. The generator lays terrain; the adapter places these onto it.

neighbours.description: field_map ids reachable from here, forming the overworld's travel graph.

epochs.description: Epoch ids from database/timeline/epochs.json. Absent means the place exists in every era -- but a settlement standing in one epoch may be a ruin in another, so prefer being explicit.

arrival.description: What the player reads on first entering. Player-facing prose, in the journal's voice.

notes.description: Reference fact for the canon reader. Not shown to the player.

climate.description: Relative likelihood of each weather, per spell. Arbitrary units, not percentages. Only the four the world actually produces are allowed: flood and full_moon are in the weather enum but are a state of the land and a phase of the moon, and nothing generates them -- see docs/decisions.md.
